posts.title: AF_VSOCK: network namespace support is here
posts.description: A missing piece for AF_VSOCK in the Linux kernel has been network namespace support. We discussed it as a future challenge during the KVM Forum 2019 talk and it was mentioned in several conference discussions since then. posts.title: vDPA: support for block devices in Linux and QEMU
posts.description: A vDPA device is a type of device that follows the virtio specification for its datapath but has a vendor-specific control path . vDPA devices can be both physically located on the hardware or emulated by software. A small vDPA parent driver in the host kernel is required only for the control path. The main advantage is the unified software stack for all vDPA devices: vhost interface (vhost-vdpa)

posts.title: SOCAT now supports AF_VSOCK
posts.description: SOCAT is a CLI utility which enables the concatenation of two sockets together. It establishes two bidirectional byte streams and transfers data between them. socat supports several address types (e.g. TCP, UDP, UNIX domain sockets, etc.) to construct the streams.
